entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq al‐Ghafiqi al‐Ishbili, known as Ibn al‐Hāʾim (fl. c. 1213), was a medieval Muslim astronomer and mathematician from Seville, Spain. He made significant contributions to the field of astronomy, particularly in the calculation of celestial bodies' orbits and the development of a new system of astronomy. Ibn al‐Hāʾim's work built upon the achievements of earlier scholars, such as Al-Biruni and Ibn Yunus, and had a lasting impact on the development of Islamic astronomy. His writings also influenced the work of later European astronomers, including Gerard of Cremona, who translated Ibn al‐Hāʾim's works into Latin. Ibn al‐Hāʾim's legacy extends beyond the realm of astronomy, as his work also had an impact on the development of mathematics and engineering. His contributions to the field of astronomy are still studied and appreciated today, and he remains an important figure in the history of Islamic scholarship.
